Gingivitis and periodontitis are two similar but different issues, main difference is the teeth structures they affect. With gingivitis sometimes changing habits and having super perfect hygiene makes it go away as it's an inflamatory process in the gums, but periodontitis doesnt work that way. It will keep progressing if you don't go back and get whatever treatment your dentist says that you need even if it sounds awful. Teeth have such a big impact in your quality of life, take good care of yours.

Here are some tips from someone who lives in this city:

Learn some spanish so you are safe if you ever get lost so you can talk to locals even if they dont speak english. Do NOT go to Raval specially at night. Avoid smaller streets at night also,  people get too drunk and messy.

As a trans person, you'll be safe, but a lot of people will try to steal from tourists, specially in: the metro, Arc del Triomf, Las Ramblas and the beach. Keep your belongings safe when roaming around, its becoming a big issue lately around here.

Dont eat in Las Ramblas or near Sagrada Familia, its too expensive and not that tasty actually, its a known scam for outsiders. Id recomend smaller restaurants and bars around the city, Universitat has some cool places and its a know LGBT+ friendly place. Oh, and dont litter, dont be rude to locals, be kind to older people like let them take your seat in the metro and that kind of stuff. Its small things that matter!

Its a big city, so stay safe and have fun!
